reference.claim_boundary: visual appearance comparison only; no biometric identity verification

target_gates.evidence: At 213x320, the near-frontal full-length view keeps both waist-to-upper-thigh outer contours visible; both high-hip regions expand beneath the belt-marked natural-waist level.
Thumbnail and native pixels show an abrupt lateral expansion immediately below the waist/high-hip line, rather than an expansion beginning only at the lower outer thighs.
On both sides, the high-hip projection continues coherently through broad outer hips into substantial upper thighs before tapering toward the boots.

The native image has a tightly cinched double-buckle belt, gathered glossy coverall fabric, a forward lean, and a wide working stance. These materially amplify the shelf-like transition, so waistband pressure and pose substitution cannot be ruled out even though the lower contour is continuous and not an isolated hip dip.

common_gates.evidence: The sole subject has clearly adult facial morphology, body scale, and professional presentation consistent with a woman in her mid-twenties or older.
One unobstructed adult face is sharp at native scale with coherent eyes, nose, lips, jaw, hairline, and natural asymmetry; no competing face appears.
Both gloved hands plausibly grip the metal wand, the arms align with the forward working posture, and both legs and booted feet remain proportional without visible fusion or extra limbs.
Both hands direct a floor-contact suction wand over displaced tesserae; the corrugated hose, wet mosaic, shallow floodwater, and condition markers make active mosaic-conservation suction legible.

Compared visually with the reference, the generated face retains a similar long oval outline, almond eye aperture and spacing, narrow lower face, nose and lip proportions, pale-neutral skin tone, center-parted dark wavy hair, and overall adult appearance. This is appearance continuity, not an identity claim.
The subject is fully covered by a long-sleeved black work coverall, gloves, utility belt, and knee-high waterproof boots throughout the full-body frame.

The reference is a head-and-shoulders portrait without waist-to-thigh geometry; the generated full-body relation is therefore evaluated from the frozen written body-shape contract, not from visible reference-body evidence.
